$comment: What every key on the page is for. Sections describe where a group of strings appears; notes single out the ones constrained by something other than meaning. Read with GLOSSARY.md.

sections.meta: Never seen on the page. These are the search result, the browser tab, and the card that appears when the address is pasted into a chat application. Written for someone who has not heard of Lukotta.
sections.ui: Controls in the header, and the link that lets a keyboard reader skip the navigation. Read aloud by screen readers, so they must say what the control does rather than name it cleverly.
sections.nav: The three header links. Features and How it works match headings further down and should use the same words as those headings; Download goes straight to the releases page.
sections.hero: The first screen. One claim, one sentence explaining it, the download link, and a technical line set in a monospace face.
sections.how: Section 01. Why a Linux virtual machine is involved, and three short steps.
sections.features: Section 02, in prose. Three short paragraphs saying what the application does. Plain statements of fact — no superlatives, no selling. The points that matter are that it takes physical drives and image files alike, that BitLocker opens with either a password or a recovery key, and that BitLocker and NTFS are written as well as read.
sections.formats: The table inside section 02: everything the application opens, grouped into encryption, filesystems and disk images, with a Read and a Write column, and a list of what is not supported. Format names are never translated.
sections.name: Section 03. One paragraph explaining the name, taken from the application's README.
sections.faq: Section 04, and the last thing on the page. Six questions, written the way a reader would type them into a search engine. These are published as structured data as well as shown on the page, so a search engine may show a question and its answer directly. Every answer must stand on its own, without the question.
sections.footer: Three links, and the copyright and licence line beneath them.

notes.meta.title: At or under 60 characters. Search results cut it off. Keyword first, brand last.
notes.meta.description: Between 70 and 165 characters. Longer is truncated mid-word.
notes.meta.ogTitle: The card title when the address is shared. May be shorter and less formal than meta.title.
notes.meta.imageAlt: Describes the Lukotta application icon, which is the shared card image.
notes.ui.skipToContent: The first thing a keyboard reader reaches. Must say plainly that it skips to the page content.
notes.ui.toTop: The spoken name of the logo, which is a link back to the top of the page.
notes.ui.switchToLight: The appearance switch's spoken name while the page is dark. It names what clicking will do, not what the page currently is.
notes.ui.switchToDark: The same switch while the page is light.
notes.hero.title: The one sentence the page is built around. Keep the full stop.
notes.hero.meta: Set in a monospace face at a small size. Contains {version}, which becomes the released version number. Keep the middle dots as separators.
notes.formats.lead: Introduces the table. The phrase 'will and will not write' is deliberate: the table has rows that are read but never written.
notes.formats.col.read: A column heading, set in capitals in a monospace face. One word if the language allows.
notes.formats.col.write: The same. These two headings sit above columns of ticks and dashes.
notes.formats.yes: Never shown on screen. It is the spoken text behind a tick, for a reader using a screen reader.
notes.formats.vmdkStream.note: Explains why this one format is read but not written. Factual, not a warning.
notes.formats.vhdx.note: The same. The application says so before the image opens, which is worth keeping.
notes.formats.specs: The whole string is a link to SPECS.md. It reads as a sentence, not as a button.
notes.formats.not.body: A list of what cannot be opened, separated by full stops. Each item is a distinct reason; keep them distinct.
notes.how.lead: The whole explanation in three sentences: macOS cannot, Linux can, so a small Linux machine does it.
notes.how.note: Explains why the drive shows a network icon in Finder. Reassurance, so it must not sound like an apology or a defect.
notes.footer.copyright: Contains {year}, replaced when the page is built, and {author}, which becomes a link to the author's own site. Both must survive, spelled exactly as they are.
notes.footer.gpl: The licence line. GNU General Public License is a proper name and is not translated, though the surrounding sentence is.
notes.faq.1.a: Names the GNU General Public License, which is not translated.
notes.faq.2.q: Phrased as a search. Keep BitLocker and Mac in it — those are the words a reader would use.
notes.faq.3.a: The distinction between what macOS does (read-only) and what Lukotta does (read and write) is the whole answer. Keep both halves.
notes.faq.5.q: Long, and deliberately so: it is the question people actually ask.
notes.faq.6.a: Says plainly that Intel Macs are not supported. Do not soften it.
notes.name.body: One paragraph. Contains {lukko} and {tta}, which become the Finnish word lukko and the Finnish ending -tta. Both are Finnish and stay as they are in every language; the placeholders must survive, spelled exactly as they are, and the sentence around them is translated.
notes.name.stress: About where the stress falls when the word is said aloud. The page shows this by setting the first syllable apart, so the sentence and the picture must agree.
notes.features.lead: One sentence saying what the application does. Flat and factual; it is not a slogan.
notes.features.body: The three facts that matter most: physical drives and image files alike, BitLocker by password or by recovery key, and BitLocker and NTFS written as well as read. All three must survive translation.
notes.features.body2: Read-only opening and reopening after a restart, mentioned once at the end rather than given their own headings.
notes.formats.not.5: A single item ending in a list of three examples after a colon.
